proposal.summary: Versions of CVAT prior to 2.0.0 contain a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability allowing the application to fetch attacker-controlled remote URLs (e.g. http://localhost:8081) when importing remote files. The issue was fixed by adding validation in 2.0.0.
proposal.cwe_quote: #CVAT is an opensource interactive video and image annotation tool for computer vision. Versions prior to 2.0.0 were found to be subject to a Server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability.

AC.quote: Validation has been added to urls used in the affected code path in version 2.0.0.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Request the vulnerable code path and proof-of-concept exploit details (server request behavior) or logs to confirm whether internal network resources can be accessed; verify whether authentication is required and reproduce on a test instance to measure impact.

evidence_quotes.claim: Description of vulnerability and versions affected
evidence_quotes.quote: #CVAT is an opensource interactive video and image annotation tool for computer vision. Versions prior to 2.0.0 were found to be subject to a Server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability.
Validation has been added to urls used in the affected code path in version 2.0.0. Users are advised to upgrade.
